runs.name: Duke Energy Corporation; NYSE DUK, SEC CIK 0001326160, Delaware, 10-K filer jointly with its Subsidiary Registrants; regulated electric utilities in two segments, Electric Utilities and Infrastructure (about 8.7 million retail customers in six states of the Southeast and Midwest) and Gas Utilities and Infrastructure; a Brookfield affiliate's $6B investment for an eventual 19.7% of Duke Energy Florida, first closing 2026-03-03; Piedmont's Tennessee gas business sold to Spire for $2.48B, 2026-03-31; the 10-K names no rival company, Southern, Dominion and AEP taken from the proxy's pay peer group as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **$121.47** (close 2026-10-16, aggregator, flagged). Shares **779,702,193** on the 10-Q cover (0001326160-26-000040); market cap $94,710M. Sovereign **5.43%**, US Treasury 30-year par yield 2026-10-16. Read from the 10-K FY2025 (0001326160-26-000014), the 10-Ks FY2023, FY2021 and FY2020, the 10-Q of 2026-06-30 (0001326160-26-000040), the proxy (0001104659-26-032443) and the 8-Ks of 2026 (Brookfield first closing, Tennessee sale, North Carolina and Progress settlements, equity units, director); lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, seven lines stated in the run file. Started 2026-10-18 (template, Step 0 and Q1 in 1e150349), stopped by a session end, resumed 2026-10-22 by one dispatched analyst. **Q1 IN**: a regulated return on a filed, planned base, $200B to $220B of capital over the decade. **Q2 IN**: the sole supplier in its territories except Ohio's competitive generation supply; EU&I decides at 90% of five-year segment income ($22,109M of $24,505M); North Carolina settled at 9.8% on 53% equity against 10.95% asked; field returns ordinary, carried to Q3 under the regulated exception. **Q3 WEIGHS AGAINST, narrowly**: about 6.5% after tax on tangible capital, added capital near the allowed return, reinvestment compulsory and above cash; owners' book return 6.7% over ten years. **Q4 IN on the accounts, WEIGHS AGAINST**: ten balance sheets 2016 to 2025, assets up 47%, debt up 78%, equity up 26%, debt 55% to 63% of capital against a 65% covenant, goodwill $19.0B or 37% of equity, retained earnings never above $5.1B; GAAP EPS $30.45 against adjusted $38.46 over 2019 to 2025, recurring "one-time" items; adjusted EPS featured, guided and paid on. **Q5 integrity IN; ability WEIGHS AGAINST** narrowly: the 2015 Dan River plea of the prior regime recorded; NTE antitrust settled March 2026 for an amount "not material"; pipeline and renewables losses outside the franchise. **Q6 WEIGHS AGAINST**: the dividend paid with raised money; $10B of common planned for 2027 to 2030; minority stakes sold above book; pay on adjusted EPS with no capital charge; guidance; political spending. **Q7 OUT**, equity-only central under Q7, The regulated utility, FY2021 to FY2025: owner cash **$3,008M a year** equity-only maintenance-only (depreciation line with nuclear fuel as the maintenance guess, stock pay, lease principal and preferred and minority payouts deducted), **$2,599M** after all spending with net long-term debt raised credited, capped at the 47% allowed debt share; -$2,647M after all spending with no credit; two CONVENTIONS of the run, the credit net of redemptions, and no credit inside the maintenance case (the double-count case shown beside, 9.26% at its top); growth cut under (f) to sales growth of 6.47% held at the 5.43% discount rate; value range **$71.06 to $109.64 a share equity-only**, the price above the top; expected return 3.18% to 4.94% at the price, below the 5.43% bond; fair price **$47.30 equity-only, central**; all-equity -$35.73, not positive; beside, $40.86 all spending with the debt credit, $37.09 with the carryforward shelter to about 2030 removed. Q8 to Q12 not reached. After the stop, facts recorded, not weighed: debt $91,238M at 2026-06-30 plus $2,000M of equity units; pre-tax interest coverage about 2.5 to 2.7 in 2021 to 2025; Brookfield's put on Florida Progress; coal ash $8B to $9B, $4.8B spent. Competitors: no rival company named in the 10-K; Southern, Dominion and AEP from the proxy's pay peer group, a CONVENTION; ten-year means, operating income on tangible assets Duke 4.32%, Southern 4.45%, Dominion 3.83%, AEP 3.98%; return on equity Duke 6.7% (lowest), Southern 11.2%, Dominion 9.7%, AEP 10.0%; peer figures XBRL transcription. Strongest evidence against: owner cash after all spending negative every year, the dividend paid with borrowing, new shares and sales of pieces; $10B of new common planned; pay on adjusted EPS without a capital charge. Commits 1e150349 (Step 0, Q1), ec455719 (resume, Q2), 4d63f248 (Q3), 1d91c88f (Q4), f643f0aa (Q5), 08dc914e (Q6), be8c7b2e (Q7 with the Q6 write-back), eac4982f (close, self-audit, gaps). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Contamination declared, items (1) to (6): commit subjects of another utility's run of 2026-10-18 and its framework-note topics, a `Test Runs/` listing of other 2026-10-18 run names, memory index lines, a Duke 10-K and 8-Ks found in `tools/_cache/duk_tmp/` and not used; none opened or used. Citations: the analyst's `check_run.py` 0 problems; the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` no missing id, 67 adjacent quoted fragments, 13 flagged and all read (filing quotes and framework headings beside an id, line-wrapped fragments, the row's words confirmed), **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) the utility credit's debt raised gross or net, and whether it is credited inside the maintenance case (net and no, confessed; the choice would decide the floor for a utility priced below about $111.53 a share on this run's arithmetic); (2) Whose tax at a cost-of-service utility, the carryforward recompute against normalised rates and credits owed back to customers; (3) the cap (f) inside ten years, the shown rate against "never above the discount rate"; (4) the named-rival rule for a franchise monopoly; (5) what Q2's regulator exception does at Q3 beyond second best. Could not get: a maintenance and growth split of capital spending (depreciation used); FY2021 and FY2022 cash-flow inputs re-read against the filed statements (XBRL used); the "Other" investing outflow; Tennessee's own earnings. Armed at the equity-only fair price.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7 (Duke Energy, DUK; regulated electricity in six states and gas; Q1 IN; Q2 IN, EU&I deciding at 90% on the franchise, North Carolina 9.8% against 10.95% asked; Q3 narrowly against, about 6.5% after tax on tangible capital, owners' book return 6.7% over ten years; Q4 accounts IN, against, debt 55% to 63% of capital against a 65% covenant, GAAP EPS $30.45 against adjusted $38.46 over 2019 to 2025; Q5 integrity IN, ability narrowly against; Q6 against, the dividend paid with raised money, $10B of common planned; owner cash $3,008M a year equity-only maintenance-only, $2,599M after all spending with the net debt credit; value range $71.06 to $109.64 equity-only vs $121.47, central 3.18% to 4.94%; fair $47.30 equity-only, armed (-$35.73 all-equity, not positive); no citation slip; not held; resumed after a stop at Q1; framework gaps for the operator: the debt credit gross or net and inside the maintenance case, Whose tax at a utility, the cap inside ten years, the named-rival rule for a monopoly, the regulator exception at Q3)
